steps.say: Materials can be solids, liquids or gases. These are the three states of matter.

figure.alt: An ice cube, a water drop and steam.

steps.say: A solid keeps its own shape. You can hold it and it does not flow.
A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container. Its volume stays the same.
A gas spreads out to fill all the space it is in. It can be squashed.
steps.show: gas: spreads out, can be squashed

steps.say: Powders like sand and salt are solids. Each tiny grain keeps its shape.

check.prompt: Which state of matter keeps its own shape?

options.why: Liquids flow and take the shape of their container.
Gases spread out to fill a space.
Only one state keeps its own shape.

hints: Think about an ice cube on a plate.
Does it spread out or stay the same?
Which state can you hold in your hand?

check.prompt: Juice takes the shape of its cup because it is a ___.
hints: It is not a solid and not a gas.
check.explanation: Juice is a liquid, so it flows and takes the shape of its container.
